subject.title: feat(chat): rewind and fork a session from a message bubble

question: Should OpenClaw expose rewind and fork as durable core gateway/session APIs, with the proposed `operator.admin` and `operator.write` permissions, rather than limit this workflow to an internal Control UI/session capability?
rationale: This is a new user-facing session-management mode that adds public protocol methods and durable transcript mutations; implementation tests cannot determine the intended long-term product and authorization contract.

options.title: Adopt the core session API
options.body: Accept rewind and fork as supported gateway lifecycle operations after real UI/session proof and current-main merge review.

options.title: Narrow the surface
options.body: Keep the UI workflow but redesign it behind an existing generic session lifecycle contract if maintainers do not want two permanent RPCs.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause the PR if the product team does not want transcript-branch manipulation as a supported chat recovery workflow.

recommendation.title: Adopt the core session API
recommendation.body: Accept rewind and fork as supported gateway lifecycle operations after real UI/session proof and current-main merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature author has the most direct implementation context and can route the final API/product decision to the relevant session and gateway owners.
